'''Shoucheng Zhang''' ({{lang-zh|s=张首晟}}; February 15, 1963 – December 1, 2018) was a Chinese-American [[physicist]] who was the JG Jackson and CJ Wood professor of [[physics]] at [[Stanford University]]. He was a [[condensed matter]] theorist known for his work on [[topological insulator]]s, the [[quantum Hall effect]], the [[quantum spin Hall effect]], [[spintronics]], and [[high-temperature superconductivity]]. According to the [[National Academy of Sciences]]:<ref name="NAS_deceased">{{cite web |date=2018 |title=Shoucheng Zhang |url=https://www.nasonline.org/directory-entry/shoucheng-zhang-jeuor4/ |access-date=December 7, 2018 |website=National Academy of Sciences |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241009193607/https://www.nasonline.org/directory-entry/shoucheng-zhang-jeuor4/ |archive-date=October 9, 2024 |url-status=live}}</ref><blockquote>He discovered a new state of matter called topological insulator in which electrons can conduct along the edge without dissipation, enabling a new generation of electronic devices with much lower power consumption. For this ground breaking work he received numerous international awards, including the Buckley Prize, the Dirac Medal and Prize, the Europhysics Prize, the Physics Frontiers Prize and the Benjamin Franklin Medal.</blockquote>

Zhang founded the [[venture capital]] firm '''Danhua Capital'''.<ref name="Yang_2018"/>

==Biography==
Zhang was born in [[Shanghai]], China in 1963. He was accepted by [[Fudan University]] in 1978 at the age of 15, and went abroad in 1980 to study at the [[Free University of Berlin]] in [[West Berlin]], where he received his B.S. degree in 1983. He then pursued his graduate studies at [[Stony Brook University]] (then referred to as [[State University of New York, Stony Brook]]). At Stony Brook, he initially studied supergravity (and earned his Ph.D. in 1987) with his advisor [[Peter van Nieuwenhuizen]], before turning to condensed matter on the advice of his personal hero, Nobel laureate [[Chen-Ning Yang]]. In the final year at Stony Brook, he switched to condensed matter physics under the supervision of [[Steven Kivelson]].

Zhang was a postdoctoral Fellow at ITP in Santa Barbara from 1987 to 1989. He then joined IBM Almaden Research Center as a Research Staff Member from 1989 to 1993. Thereafter, he joined Stanford University as assistant professor of physics. Beginning in 2004, he concurrently held (by courtesy appointment) titles of Professor of [[applied physics|Applied Physics]] and Professor of [[electrical engineering|Electrical Engineering]] at Stanford University. In 2007, the "[[quantum spin Hall effect]]" discovered by Zhang was named one of the "Top Ten Important Scientific Breakthroughs in the World" by [[Science (journal)|''Science Magazine'']]. In 2010, he was named the J. G. Jackson and C. J. Wood Professor in Physics.<ref>{{cite web |title=Shoucheng Zhang |url=https://physics.stanford.edu/people/faculty/shoucheng-zhang |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130118075744/https://physics.stanford.edu/people/faculty/shoucheng-zhang |archive-date=January 18, 2013 |website=Stanford University |department=Department of Physics}}</ref>

In 2009, Zhang was chosen to be a part of an expert panel for the [[Thousand Talents Program (China)|Thousand Talents Program]]. In 2013, Zhang created Danhua Capital, a [[venture capital]] firm, which raised $434.5 million across two funds.<ref name="Yang_2018">{{cite news |last1=Yang |first1=Yingzhi |last2=Huang |first2=Zheping |date=December 6, 2018 |title=Zhang Shoucheng, Stanford physicist and tech venture capitalist dies after 'a battle with depression' |url=https://www.scmp.com/tech/article/2176729/zhang-shoucheng-stanford-physicist-and-tech-venture-capitalist-dies-after |access-date=December 6, 2018 |work=South China Morning Post |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181206095209/https://www.scmp.com/tech/article/2176729/zhang-shoucheng-stanford-physicist-and-tech-venture-capitalist-dies-after |archive-date=December 6, 2018 |url-status=live}}</ref> Danhua Capital's major investors include state-owned Beijing government enterprise Zhongguancun Development Group (ZDG), which has been linked to the Chinese technology transfer program [[Made in China 2025]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Gertz |first=Bill |date=December 12, 2018 |title=Physicist linked to China program |url=https://www.washingtontimes.com/news/2018/dec/12/physicist-linked-to-china-program/ |access-date=December 14, 2018 |work=Washington Times |language=en |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181213151627/https://www.washingtontimes.com/news/2018/dec/12/physicist-linked-to-china-program/ |archive-date=December 13, 2018 |url-status=live}}</ref> He also served as an independent non-executive director at Lenovo Group and at Meitu.<ref>{{cite web |title=Renowned Stanford Physicist Shoucheng Zhang Dies at 55 |url=https://www.caixinglobal.com/2018-12-06/renowned-stanford-physicist-shoucheng-zhang-dies-at-55-101356210.html |access-date=December 6, 2018 |website=Caixin Global |language=en |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181206235039/https://www.caixinglobal.com/2018-12-06/renowned-stanford-physicist-shoucheng-zhang-dies-at-55-101356210.html |archive-date=December 6, 2018 |url-status=live}}</ref>

Zhang's wife Barbara is a software engineer at IBM. They met in kindergarten, in Shanghai. Together they have two children, a son Brian and a daughter Stephanie.<ref>{{cite news |last=Zhang |first=Qidong |date=February 21, 2014 |title=Shoucheng Zhang: Maotai and a possible Nobel Prize await this scientist |url=http://usa.chinadaily.com.cn/epaper/2014-02/21/content_17295558.htm |access-date=December 7, 2018 |work=China Daily |quote=Zhang's wife Barbara, whom he has known since kindergarten, is a software engineer at IBM. |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181209123452/http://usa.chinadaily.com.cn/epaper/2014-02/21/content_17295558.htm |archive-date=December 9, 2018 |url-status=live}}</ref>

Zhang died in San Francisco on December 1, 2018, at the age of 55, in an apparent suicide. His family said in a statement that he died "after fighting a battle with [[major depressive disorder|depression]]."<ref>{{cite web |last=Han |first=Shengjiang |date=December 6, 2018 |script-title=zh:美国华裔物理学家张首晟教授去世，终年55岁 |url=https://www.thepaper.cn/newsDetail_forward_2711884 |access-date=December 6, 2018 |website=[[The Paper (newspaper)|The Paper]] |lang=zh |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181206102414/https://www.thepaper.cn/newsDetail_forward_2711884 |archive-date=December 6, 2018 |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last=Castelvecchi |first=Davide |date=December 8, 2018 |title=Topological-physics pioneer Shoucheng Zhang dies: Theoretical physicist was among the first to predict that the phenomenon of topology could lead to exotic states of matter. |url=https://www.nature.com/articles/d41586-018-07709-y |journal=[[Nature (journal)|Nature]] |doi=10.1038/d41586-018-07709-y |s2cid=126400522 |url-access=subscription |access-date=December 9, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181211195701/https://www.nature.com/articles/d41586-018-07709-y |archive-date=December 11, 2018 |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Garisto |first1=Daniel |date=December 10, 2018 |title=Shoucheng Zhang 1963-2018 |url=https://www.aps.org/publications/apsnews/updates/zhang.cfm |access-date=May 20, 2019 |work=[[American Physical Society]] |language=en |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190703140659/https://www.aps.org/publications/apsnews/updates/zhang.cfm |archive-date=July 3, 2019 |url-status=live}}</ref>

==Scientific achievements==
Zhang was one of the founders of the field of topological insulators. He made one of the first theoretical proposals of the quantum spin Hall effect. Soon after the initial theoretical proposal, his group theoretically predicted the first realistic quantum spin Hall material in HgTe quantum wells.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Bernevig |first1=B. Andrei |last2=Hughes |first2=Taylor L. |last3=Zhang |first3=Shou-Cheng |year=2006 |title=Quantum spin Hall effect and topological phase transition in HgTe quantum wells. |journal=Science |volume=314 |issue=5806 |pages=1757–1761 |arxiv=cond-mat/0611399 |bibcode=2006Sci...314.1757B |doi=10.1126/science.1133734 |pmid=17170299 |s2cid=7295726}}</ref> This prediction was soon confirmed experimentally,<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=König |first1=Markus |last2=Wiedmann |first2=Steffen |last3=Brüne |first3=Christoph |last4=Roth |first4=Andreas |last5=Buhmann |first5=Hartmut |last6=Molenkamp |first6=Laurens W. |last7=Qi |first7=Xiao-Liang |last8=Zhang |first8=Shou-Cheng |date=November 2, 2007 |title=Quantum Spin Hall Insulator State in HgTe Quantum Wells |url=https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/science.1148047 |journal=Science |language=en |volume=318 |issue=5851 |pages=766–770 |doi=10.1126/science.1148047 |pmid=17885096 |arxiv=0710.0582 |bibcode=2007Sci...318..766K |issn=0036-8075 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231129092058/https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/science.1148047 |archive-date=November 29, 2023 |access-date=October 20, 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref> launching worldwide research activities. Subsequently, his group predicted numerous novel topological states of matter and topological effects, including the [[bismuth selenide|Bi<sub>2</sub>Se<sub>3</sub>]] family of 3D [[topological insulator]]s,<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Zhang |first1=Haijun |last2=Liu |first2=Chao-Xing |last3=Qi |first3=Xiao-Liang |last4=Dai |first4=Xi |last5=Fang |first5=Zhong |last6=Zhang |first6=Shou-Cheng |date=June 2009 |title=Topological insulators in Bi2Se3, Bi2Te3 and Sb2Te3 with a single Dirac cone on the surface |url=https://www.nature.com/articles/nphys1270 |journal=Nature Physics |language=en |volume=5 |issue=6 |pages=438–442 |doi=10.1038/nphys1270 |issn=1745-2473 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250212075851/https://www.nature.com/articles/nphys1270 |archive-date=February 12, 2025 |access-date=October 20, 2026 |url-status=live|url-access=subscription }}</ref> the topological magneto-electric effect,<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Qi |first1=Xiao-Liang |last2=Hughes |first2=Taylor L. |last3=Zhang |first3=Shou-Cheng |date=November 2008 |title=Topological field theory of time-reversal invariant insulators |url=https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRevB.78.195424 |journal=Physical Review B |language=en |volume=78 |issue=19 |article-number=195424 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevB.78.195424 |arxiv=0802.3537 |bibcode=2008PhRvB..78s5424Q |issn=1098-0121}}</ref> the quantum anomalous Hall effect in [[magnetic topological insulator]]s, time-reversal invariant topological superconductors, and the realization of a chiral topological superconductor and of chiral [[Majorana fermion]]s using the [[quantum anomalous Hall effect|quantum anomalous Hall]] state in proximity with a superconductor. Most of these predicted properties have now been experimentally observed.

Earlier, Zhang also made significant contributions to other areas of physics. He and collaborators derived a topological ([[Chern–Simons form]]) quantum field theoretic description of the novel properties of fractional quantum Hall liquids,<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Zhang |first=Shou Cheng |date=January 1992 |title=The Chern–Simons–Landau–Ginzburg Theory of the Fractional Quantum Hall Effect |url=https://www.worldscientific.com/doi/abs/10.1142/S0217979292000037 |journal=International Journal of Modern Physics B |language=en |volume=06 |issue=1 |pages=25–58 |doi=10.1142/S0217979292000037 |issn=0217-9792 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230228214350/https://www.worldscientific.com/doi/abs/10.1142/S0217979292000037 |archive-date=February 28, 2023 |access-date=October 20, 2026 |url-status=live|url-access=subscription }}</ref> and proposed a global phase diagram for the quantum Hall states with many features that have had since been experimentally observed. He generalized the theory of fractional quantum Hall effect to higher dimensions and related it to fundamental particle physics. He also proposed an influential theory of [[high-temperature superconductivity]] based on an extended symmetry principle.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Zhang |first=Shou-Cheng |date=February 1997 |title=A Unified Theory Based on SO (5) Symmetry of Superconductivity and Antiferromagnetism |url=https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/science.275.5303.1089 |journal=Science |language=en |volume=275 |issue=5303 |pages=1089–1096 |doi=10.1126/science.275.5303.1089 |pmid=9027303 |bibcode=1997Sci...275.1089Z |issn=0036-8075 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250629101753/https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/science.275.5303.1089 |archive-date=June 29, 2025 |access-date=October 20, 2026 |url-status=live|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

In early 2000, Zhang and collaborators revitalized the field of spintronics by proposing an intrinsic spin Hall effect and relating it to geometrical phases in quantum mechanics. This proposal stimulated extensive theoretical and experimental work, and also contributed to later developments concerning the quantum spin Hall effect and topological insulators more generally.

Between the years 2010–2015, Zhang and his group of physicists at [[Stanford University]] wrote three theoretical papers where they successfully showed how to test [[Ettore Majorana]]'s theory of [[Majorana fermion]], or what had previously been only a scientific hypothesis that a particle can be its own [[antiparticle]], without the need of external forces having the same mass with the opposite charge of the electron.<ref>{{cite AV media |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MozDSajpLTY |title=Quantum Computing, AI and Blockchain: The Future of IT |date=June 6, 2018 |publisher=Talks at Google |via=YouTube |at=7:42 |access-date=December 5, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181209224806/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MozDSajpLTY |archive-date=December 9, 2018 |url-status=live}}</ref>

==Honors and awards==
Zhang was a fellow of the [[American Physical Society]] and a fellow of the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]]. He received the [[Guggenheim fellowship]] in 2007, the Alexander von Humboldt Research Prize in 2009, the [[Europhysics Prize]] in 2010,<ref name="Johnston_2010">{{cite web |last=Johnston |first=Hamish |date=June 21, 2010 |title=Topological quintet bags Europhysics prize |url=https://physicsworld.com/a/topological-quintet-bags-europhysics-prize/ |access-date=December 7, 2018 |website=Physics World |quote=Five physicists who brought us the quantum spin-Hall effect and topological insulators have been awarded this year's Europhysics Prize from the European Physical Society's condensed-matter division. The winners are Shoucheng Zhang of Stanford University; Charles Kane and Eugene Mele of the University of Pennsylvania; and Hartmut Buhmann and Laurens Molenkamp of Würzburg University in Germany. |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181209123715/https://physicsworld.com/a/topological-quintet-bags-europhysics-prize/ |archive-date=December 9, 2018 |url-status=live}}</ref> the [[Oliver Buckley Prize]] in 2012, the [[Dirac Medal (ICTP)|Dirac Medal]] and Prize in 2012, the Physics Frontiers Prize in 2013, the "Nobel-class" Citation Laureates by Thomson Reuters in 2014,<ref>{{cite web |last=Orwig |first=Jessica |date=September 25, 2014 |title=Meet The Scientists Who Could Win This Year's Physics Nobel Prize |url=https://www.businessinsider.com/computing-physics-nobel-prize-candidates-2014-9 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230425100836/https://www.businessinsider.com/computing-physics-nobel-prize-candidates-2014-9 |archive-date=April 25, 2023 |website=Business Insider}}</ref> and the [[Benjamin Franklin Medal (Franklin Institute)|Benjamin Franklin Medal]] in 2015. He was identified as one of the top candidates for the Nobel Prize by Thomson Reuters in 2014.<ref name="Thomson Reuters_2014">{{cite press release |title=Thomson Reuters Predicts 2014 Nobel Laureates, Researchers Forecast for Nobel Recognition |date=September 20, 2014 |publisher=Thomson Reuters |url=http://thomsonreuters.com/press-releases/092014/2014-nobel-laureates-predictions |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140929225027/http://thomsonreuters.com/press-releases/092014/2014-nobel-laureates-predictions |archive-date=September 29, 2014}}</ref> He was elected as a member of the US [[National Academy of Sciences]] in 2015.
